items.label: Setup S-1
items.nl: A finite observational experiment with a categorical confounder. One unit is \(O=(X,A,Y)\in[d]\times\{0,1\}^2\) with \([d]=\{1,\ldots,d\}\), \(d\ge2\); generic indices are \(i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\), \(x\in[d]\), \(a,y\in\{0,1\}\), and \(j=(x,a,y)\in\mathcal J_d=[d]\times\{0,1\}^2\). An observed law \(\mathbb P\) is described by its atom masses \(q_{ay,x}=\mathbb P(X=x,A=a,Y=y)\) (also written \(q_j\)), collected into four-vectors \(q_x\); these determine the cell mass \(p_x\), the propensity \(\pi_x\) and the outcome regressions \(\mu_{ax}\) on occupied cells. For a public overlap floor \(0<\epsilon\le1/2\), which may vary with \(n\) and \(d\), \(\mathcal D_{d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{obs}}\) is the class of observed laws whose occupied cells satisfy \(\epsilon\le\pi_x\le1-\epsilon\); cell masses are otherwise unrestricted and null cells are allowed. The sample is \(n\) independent draws \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\) from \(\mathbb P\). The target is \(\Psi(\mathbb P)=\sum_xp_x\max_a\mu_{ax}\), the loss is squared error, and \(\mathfrak R_{n,d,\epsilon}\) is the infimum over all measurable estimators of the worst-case risk over \(\mathcal D_{d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{obs}}\). The rate scale is \(L_d=\log(ed)\), and \(c_\star\le C_\star\) denote universal numerical constants independent of \(n,d,\epsilon\).

items.label: Setup S-2
items.nl: A finite binary potential-outcome overlay on the same alphabet. A full-data law \(P\) is a law of \((X,A,Y,Y(0),Y(1))\) with \(X\in[d]\) and \(A,Y,Y(0),Y(1)\in\{0,1\}\); its observed margin \(\operatorname{Obs}(P)\) is the law of \((X,A,Y)\). The causal target is the unrestricted oracle value \(V^\star(P)=E_P[\max_aE_P\{Y(a)\mid X\}]\), and the causal completion class \(\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon}\) collects the full-data laws satisfying consistency \(Y=Y(A)\) and armwise conditional exchangeability \(Y(a)\perp A\mid X\) whose observed margin lies in \(\mathcal D_{d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{obs}}\).

items.label: Setup S-3
items.nl: The four-cell analytic functional and the capped-Poisson armwise Jackson--factorial construction. For \(u,v\in\mathbb R_+^4\) with coordinates \(u_{ay}\), put \(s_a(u)=u_{a0}+u_{a1}\), \(s(u)=s_0(u)+s_1(u)\), \(D_a(u)=\max\{s_a(u),\epsilon s(u)\}\), the armwise perturbations \(\Delta_a\), and the anchored extension \(F_\epsilon(u)\). The deterministic split uses \(n_{\mathrm p}=\lfloor n/2\rfloor\), \(n_{\mathrm e}=n-n_{\mathrm p}\), index sets \(I_{\mathrm p},I_{\mathrm e}\), histograms \(N^{\mathrm p},N^{\mathrm e}\) with coordinates \(N_j^{\mathrm p},N_j^{\mathrm e}\), multi-indices \(\boldsymbol h,\boldsymbol t,\boldsymbol r\), a centering vector \(b\), and the centered multinomial factorial statistic \(U_{\boldsymbol h}(N^{\mathrm e};b)\). Universal constants \(H_0,\kappa,D_0\) calibrate the degree \(K_n\), the intensity \(m=n/8\), and the normalized Jackson kernel \(J_{K_n}\). An auxiliary capped count \(\mathsf M\sim\operatorname{Pois}(n/4)\) and fair marks \(\mathsf B_i\) produce pilot and evaluation counts \(N'_{ay,x},N_{ay,x}\); full-sample counts \(N_x,N_{ax},S_{ax}\) drive the bounded-alphabet branch. The pilot yields \(c_{ay,x},h_{ay,x},\ell_{ay,x},u_{ay,x},r_{ay,x}\), the center \(b_x\) and rectangle \(Q_x\); the tensor Jackson polynomial \(P_{x,K_n}\) has centered coefficients \(\beta_{x,\boldsymbol\alpha}\), lifted by \(U_k(N;\zeta)\) to \(Z_x\), clipped with scale \(S_x^{\mathrm{aw}}\) built from \(R_{a,x}\) and \(w_{a,x}\) to \(T_x\), summed and projected to \(\widetilde V\), and Rao--Blackwellized to \(\widehat V_{n,d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{AF}}\).

items.label: Setup S-4
items.nl: The scalar approximation problem and the normalized boundary-propensity lower experiment. For an integer degree \(K\ge2\), an endpoint \(2\le M\le K^2\) and \(0\le\epsilon\le1/2\), scalar intensities \(z,w\in[0,M]\) carry the weighted positive-part functional \(\phi_\epsilon(z)=\{(1-\epsilon)+\epsilon z\}(z-1)_+/(1+z)\), the weighted best-approximation error \(\mathcal E_{K,M,\epsilon}^{w}\), and the normalized constrained moment-prior separation \(\Delta_{K,M,\epsilon}\); \(\mathscr H^{w}\) is the common-atom completion map: for finite nonnegative measures \(\sigma_+,\sigma_-\) with finite first moments and \(t=\sigma_+(\mathbb R)<1\), \(u=\int z\,d\sigma_+\) and \(z_0=(1-u)/(1-t)\), it returns \((\sigma_-+(1-t)_+\delta_{z_0},\,\sigma_++(1-t)_+\delta_{z_0})\), asserting no output property for arbitrary inputs; and \(c_w,K_0\) are universal constants of the approximation comparison. A vector \(\mathbf z\in[0,M]^d\) indexes the normalized sparse observed law \(\mathbb P_{\mathbf z}^{\mathrm{sp}}\) with normalizer \(S(\mathbf z)\). The auxiliary product-Poisson comparison experiment has total-mean inflation \(B>2\), reference intensity \(z_\star=M/2\), one-cell likelihood ratios \(L_z\), and exact Gram coefficient \(\alpha\).

items.label: Definition P-1
items.nl: \(\mathcal D_{d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{obs}}:=\{\mathbb P:\mathbb P\text{ is a law on }[d]\times\{0,1\}^2,\ q_{a1,x}=p_x\pi_x^a(1-\pi_x)^{1-a}\mu_{ax},\ q_{a0,x}=p_x\pi_x^a(1-\pi_x)^{1-a}(1-\mu_{ax})\text{ for every }x\in[d],a\in\{0,1\},\ p_x\ge0,\sum_{x=1}^dp_x=1,\mu_{ax}\in[0,1],\text{ and }\mathrm{ass:shrinking\mbox{-}overlap}\text{ holds on every }p_x>0\}\) for every \(n\ge1\), \(d\ge2\), and \(0<\epsilon\le1/2\).

items.label: Definition P-2
items.nl: \(\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon}:=\{P:P\text{ is a law of }(X,A,Y,Y(0),Y(1)),\ P\text{ satisfies }\mathrm{ass:consistency}\text{ and }\mathrm{ass:conditional\mbox{-}exchangeability},\text{ and }\operatorname{Obs}(P)\in\mathcal D_{d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{obs}}\}\) for every \(n\ge1\), \(d\ge2\), and \(0<\epsilon\le1/2\).

items.label: Definition P-3
items.nl: For \(\mathbb P\in\mathcal D_{d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{obs}}\), set \(\Psi(\mathbb P)=\sum_{x=1}^dp_x\max_{a\in\{0,1\}}\mu_{ax}\), with each null-cell summand defined as zero.

items.label: Definition P-5
items.nl: For \(u\in\mathbb R_+^4\), define \(s_a(u)=u_{a0}+u_{a1}\), \(s(u)=s_0(u)+s_1(u)\), \(D_a(u)=\max\{s_a(u),\epsilon s(u)\}\), and \(F_\epsilon(u)=\max_a s(u)u_{a1}/D_a(u)\) when \(u\ne0\), with \(F_\epsilon(0)=0\).

items.label: Definition P-6
items.nl: Set \(n_{\mathrm p}=\lfloor n/2\rfloor\), \(n_{\mathrm e}=n-n_{\mathrm p}\), \(I_{\mathrm p}=\{1,\ldots,n_{\mathrm p}\}\), and \(I_{\mathrm e}=\{n_{\mathrm p}+1,\ldots,n\}\). For \(j\in\mathcal J_d\), set \(N_j^{\mathrm p}=\sum_{i\in I_{\mathrm p}}\mathbf 1\{O_i=j\}\) and \(N_j^{\mathrm e}=\sum_{i\in I_{\mathrm e}}\mathbf 1\{O_i=j\}\). Write \((m)_k=m(m-1)\cdots(m-k+1)\), \((m)_0=1\), and, for \(|\boldsymbol h|\le n_{\mathrm e}\), define \[U_{\boldsymbol h}(N^{\mathrm e};b)=\sum_{\boldsymbol t\le\boldsymbol h}\left\{\prod_{j\in\mathcal J_d}\binom{h_j}{t_j}(-b_j)^{h_j-t_j}\right\}\frac{\prod_{j\in\mathcal J_d}(N_j^{\mathrm e})_{t_j}}{(n_{\mathrm e})_{|\boldsymbol t|}}.\]

items.label: Definition P-7
items.nl:
Put \(L=L_d=\log(ed)\), \(m=n/8\), and \(K_n=\max\{2,\lfloor\kappa L\rfloor\}\).  If \(d<D_0\), let \(\widehat V_{n,d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{AF}}\) be the projection onto \([0,1]\) of
\[
 \sum_{x=1}^d\frac{N_x}{n}\max_{a\in\{0,1\}}
 \left\{\frac{S_{ax}}{N_{ax}}\mathbf 1\{N_{ax}>0\}\right\},
 \quad
 N_x=\sum_{i=1}^n\mathbf 1\{X_i=x\},\quad
 N_{ax}=\sum_{i=1}^n\mathbf 1\{X_i=x,A_i=a\},\quad
 S_{ax}=\sum_{i=1}^nY_i\mathbf 1\{X_i=x,A_i=a\}.
\]
If \(d\ge D_0\) and \(n\epsilon<d/L\), set \(\widehat V_{n,d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{AF}}=1/2\).  On the remaining branch, independently of the observations draw \(\mathsf M\sim\operatorname{Pois}(n/4)\).  On \(\{\mathsf M\le n\}\), independently mark the observations \(O_1,\ldots,O_{\mathsf M}\) by \(\mathsf B_i\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\), and let \(N'_{ay,x}\) and \(N_{ay,x}\) be the category counts among marks one and zero, respectively.  Define
\[
 c_{ay,x}=\frac{N'_{ay,x}}m,\qquad
 h_{ay,x}=H_0\left\{\sqrt{\frac{c_{ay,x}L}{m}}+\frac Lm\right\},
\]
\[
 \ell_{ay,x}=(c_{ay,x}-h_{ay,x})_+,qquad
 u_{ay,x}=c_{ay,x}+h_{ay,x},\qquad
 b_{ay,x}=\frac{\ell_{ay,x}+u_{ay,x}}2,qquad
 r_{ay,x}=\frac{u_{ay,x}-\ell_{ay,x}}2,
\]
and \(Q_x=\prod_{a,y}[\ell_{ay,x},u_{ay,x}]\).  Let
\[
 J_{K_n}(t)=c_{K_n}^{\mathrm J}
 \left\{\frac{\sin(K_nt/2)}{\sin(t/2)}\right\}^{4},
 \qquad \int_{-\pi}^{\pi}J_{K_n}(t)\,dt=1,
\]
where removable values are filled continuously and \(c_{K_n}^{\mathrm J}>0\) is the unique normalizing constant.  With componentwise multiplication denoted by \(\odot\), define the algebraic polynomial \(P_{x,K_n}\) on \(Q_x\) by
\[
 P_{x,K_n}(b_x+r_x\odot\cos\theta)
 =\int_{[-\pi,\pi]^4}
 F_\epsilon\!\left(b_x+r_x\odot\cos(\theta+\tau)\right)
 \prod_{a,y}J_{K_n}(\tau_{ay})\,d\tau .
\]
It has coordinate degree at most \(D=2(K_n-1)\).  Expand it uniquely as
\[
 P_{x,K_n}(v)-F_\epsilon(b_x)
 =\sum_{\boldsymbol\alpha\in\{0,\ldots,D\}^4}
 \beta_{x,\boldsymbol\alpha}
 \prod_{a,y}\left(\frac{v_{ay}-b_{ay,x}}{r_{ay,x}}\right)^{\alpha_{ay}}.
\]
For an integer \(k\ge0\), put
\[
 U_k(N;\zeta)=\sum_{t=0}^k\binom kt(-\zeta)^{k-t}\frac{(N)_t}{m^t},
\]
and set
\[
 Z_x=F_\epsilon(b_x)+
 \sum_{\boldsymbol\alpha\in\{0,\ldots,D\}^4}
 \beta_{x,\boldsymbol\alpha}
 \prod_{a,y}\frac{U_{\alpha_{ay}}(N_{ay,x};b_{ay,x})}
 {r_{ay,x}^{\alpha_{ay}}}.
\]
Finally define
\[
 R_{a,x}=r_{a0,x}+r_{a1,x},\qquad
 w_{a,x}=1+\frac{s(b_x)}{D_a(b_x)},\qquad
 S_x^{\mathrm{aw}}=2\sum_{a=0}^1w_{a,x}R_{a,x},
\]
\[
 T_x=\Pi_{[F_\epsilon(b_x)-d^{1/4}S_x^{\mathrm{aw}},\,
                    F_\epsilon(b_x)+d^{1/4}S_x^{\mathrm{aw}}]}(Z_x),
 \qquad
 \widetilde V=\Pi_{[0,1]}\left(\sum_{x=1}^dT_x\right).
\]
On \(\{\mathsf M>n\}\), define \(\widetilde V=0\).  The active-branch estimator is the Rao--Blackwellization
\[
 \widehat V_{n,d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{AF}}
 =E[\widetilde V\mid O_1,\ldots,O_n],
\]
where the conditional expectation integrates only \(\mathsf M\) and the marks.  Thus \(\widehat V_{n,d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{AF}}\) is a deterministic measurable function of the observed sample.

items.label: Definition P-8
items.nl: \(\mathcal E_{K,M,\epsilon}^{w}:=\inf_{P\in\mathbb R_K[z]}\sup_{0\le z\le M}|\phi_\epsilon(z)-P(z)|/(1+z)\), where \(\mathbb R_K[z]\) is the set of real polynomials of degree at most \(K\).

items.label: Definition P-9
items.nl: For \(\mathbf z\in[0,M]^d\), first set unnormalized masses \(\widetilde q_{11,x}=\epsilon(1-\epsilon)z_x/d\), \(\widetilde q_{10,x}=\epsilon(1-\epsilon)/d\), and \(\widetilde q_{00,x}=\widetilde q_{01,x}=\{(1-\epsilon)^2+\epsilon^2z_x\}/(2d)\). Their sum is \(S(\mathbf z)\); define \(\mathbb P_{\mathbf z}^{\mathrm{sp}}(X=x,A=a,Y=y)=\widetilde q_{ay,x}/S(\mathbf z)\).

items.label: Definition P-10
items.nl: For finite nonnegative measures \(\sigma_+,\sigma_-\) on \(\mathbb R\), each with finite first moment and with \(t=\sigma_+(\mathbb R)<1\), set \(t=\sigma_+(\mathbb R)\), \(u=\int z\,d\sigma_+(z)\), and \(z_0=(1-u)/(1-t)\). Define \(\mathscr H^w(\sigma_+,\sigma_-)=(\sigma_-+(1-t)_+\delta_{z_0},\,\sigma_++(1-t)_+\delta_{z_0})\). This definition is only the common-atom completion map and asserts no probability, support, moment, or dual-optimality property for arbitrary inputs. Theorem \(\mathrm{thm:weighted\mbox{-}separation\mbox{-}and\mbox{-}frontier}\) proves those properties for its constructed packet inputs under the theorem's stated premises.

items.label: Definition P-11
items.nl:
For integers \(K\geq2\), real numbers \(2\leq M\leq K^2\), and \(0\leq\epsilon\leq1/2\), let \(\mathfrak N_{K,M}\) be the set of pairs \((\nu_0,\nu_1)\) of probability measures on \([0,M]\) such that
\[
 \int z\,d\nu_0(z)=\int z\,d\nu_1(z)=1,
 \qquad
 \int z^j\,d\nu_0(z)=\int z^j\,d\nu_1(z)
 \quad (j=0,1,\ldots,K).
\]
Define the normalized constrained prior separation by
\[
 \Delta_{K,M,\epsilon}
 :=\sup_{(\nu_0,\nu_1)\in\mathfrak N_{K,M}}
 \left|\int_0^M\phi_\epsilon(z)\,d\{\nu_1-\nu_0\}(z)\right|.
\]

items.label: Definition P-12
items.nl: Along admissible nonsaturated sequences with \(d\to\infty\), \(\epsilon\to0\), and \(d/[n\epsilon L_d]\to0\), consider the normalized risk \[(n\epsilon L_d/d)\mathfrak R_{n,d,\epsilon}.\] Does there exist one finite positive constant to which the whole normalized-risk sequence converges for every admissible path? Alternatively, do there exist two admissible overlap paths whose whole normalized-risk sequences converge to distinct finite positive constants? These alternatives need not be exhaustive: a normalized-risk sequence may fail to converge along one path. A cone-constrained approximation--moment saddle for the boundary-propensity likelihood and an observable no-loss transfer are possible research directions, not part of either formal question.

items.label: Assumption A-1
items.nl: For each \(\mathbb P\in\mathcal D_{d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{obs}}\), the observations \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\) are independent and have common law \(\mathbb P\).

items.label: Lemma L-1
items.nl:
For nonnegative four-vectors \(u,v\) with \(v\ne0\), let \(\Delta_a=\sum_{y=0}^1|u_{ay}-v_{ay}|\).  Then
\[
 |F_\epsilon(u)-F_\epsilon(v)|
 \leq2\sum_{a=0}^1\Delta_a
 +2\sum_{a=0}^1\frac{s(v)}{D_a(v)}\Delta_a.
\]
If \(v=q_x\) for \(\mathbb P\in\mathcal D_{d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{obs}}\) and \(p_x>0\), then
\[
 \sum_{a=0}^1\frac{p_x}{s_a(v)}\sum_{y=0}^1\sqrt{v_{ay}}
 \leq 2\sqrt2\sqrt{\frac{p_x}{\epsilon}}.
\]

items.label: Lemma L-2
items.nl: For every \(\mathbf z\in[0,M]^d\), the construction \(\mathbb P_{\mathbf z}^{\mathrm{sp}}\) is a probability law in \(\mathcal D_{d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{obs}}\), with \(p_x=\{1-\epsilon+\epsilon z_x\}/[dS(\mathbf z)]\), \(\pi_x=\epsilon(1-\epsilon)(1+z_x)/(1-\epsilon+\epsilon z_x)\), \(\mu_{0x}=1/2\), \(\mu_{1x}=z_x/(1+z_x)\), and \[\Psi(\mathbb P_{\mathbf z}^{\mathrm{sp}})=\frac12+\frac{1}{2dS(\mathbf z)}\sum_{x=1}^d\phi_\epsilon(z_x).\] In the product-Poisson experiment with unnormalized means \(Bn\widetilde q_{ay,x}\), the exact one-cell likelihoods satisfy \[E_{z_\star}[L_zL_w]=\exp\{\alpha(z-z_\star)(w-z_\star)\},\qquad \alpha=\frac{Bn}{d}\left\{\frac{\epsilon(1-\epsilon)}{z_\star}+\frac{\epsilon^4}{(1-\epsilon)^2+\epsilon^2z_\star}\right\}\le\frac{2Bn\epsilon}{dM}.\]

items.label: Lemma L-3
items.nl:
For every integer \(N\geq2\), let
\[
 \mathcal J_N(u)=c_N\left\{\frac{\sin(Nu/2)}{\sin(u/2)}\right\}^{4},
 \qquad
 \int_{-\pi}^{\pi}\mathcal J_N(u)\,\frac{du}{2\pi}=1,
\]
with removable values filled continuously, put \(L=4N\), and set
\(k_N(u)=\mathcal J_N(u)\cos(Lu)\).  If
\(\widehat h(j)=\int_{-\pi}^{\pi}h(u)e^{-iju}\,du/(2\pi)\), define
\[
 a_j^{\pm}=
 \begin{cases}
 \widehat{\mathcal J_N}(j)/(L\pm j)^2,& |j|\leq2N-2,\\
 0,& |j|>2N-2,
 \end{cases}
 \qquad
 (\delta a)_j=a_{j+1}-a_j.
\]
There is a universal constant \(C<\infty\) such that
\[
 \sum_{j\in\mathbb Z}|\delta^2a_j^{\pm}|\leq \frac{C}{N^3}.
\]
All endpoint differences are included by the displayed zero extension.  Moreover, \(k_N\) has Fourier support in
\[
 \{r\in\mathbb Z:2N+2\leq |r|\leq6N-2\}.
\]
Consequently its unique zero-mean \(2\pi\)-periodic twice antiderivative \(G_N\), defined by \(G_N''=k_N\), satisfies, for every real \(u\),
\[
 \frac{c}{N}\leq |G_N(0)|\leq\frac{C}{N},
 \qquad
 |G_N(u)|\leq\frac{C}{N\{1+N\|u\|_{\mathbb T}\}^2},
 \qquad
 \int_{-\pi}^{\pi}|G_N(u)|\,\frac{du}{2\pi}\leq\frac{C}{N^2},
\]
where \(c>0\) is universal and \(\|u\|_{\mathbb T}=\min_{r\in\mathbb Z}|u-2\pi r|\).

items.label: Theorem T-1
items.nl: Every \(\mathbb P\in\mathcal D_{d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{obs}}\) admits a completion \(P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon}\) with \(\operatorname{Obs}(P)=\mathbb P\), and every \(P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon}\) satisfies \(V^\star(P)=\Psi\{\operatorname{Obs}(P)\}\). For the four-vector \(q_x\), \(F_\epsilon(q_x)=p_x\max_a\mu_{ax}\), including the null-cell convention.

items.label: Theorem T-2
items.nl:
There are universal choices of \(H_0\), \(\kappa\), \(D_0\), and \(C_\star<\infty\) such that, for every \(n\ge1\), \(d\ge2\), and \(0<\epsilon\le1/2\), the estimator \(\widehat V_{n,d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{AF}}\) in \(\mathrm{def:armwise\mbox{-}estimator}\) is a deterministic fully observed statistic and
\[
 \sup_{\mathbb P\in\mathcal D_{d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{obs}}}
 E_{\mathbb P}\!\left[
 \{\widehat V_{n,d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{AF}}-\Psi(\mathbb P)\}^2
 \right]
 \le C_\star\min\left\{1,\frac{d}{n\epsilon L_d}\right\}.
\]
The bound permits arbitrary unknown cell masses, unknown unequal propensities, null cells, boundary outcome means, and exact treatment-effect ties.

items.label: Theorem T-3
items.nl: there is a universal \(c_\star>0\) such that, for every \(n\ge1\), \(d\ge2\), and \(0<\epsilon\le1/2\), \[\mathfrak R_{n,d,\epsilon}\ge c_\star\min\left\{1,\frac{d}{n\epsilon L_d}\right\}.\] The proof must use the full likelihood in Lemma 4, normalize the moment priors without conditioning on a simplex event, and splice a boundary-propensity dense moment-matching experiment with a rare-arm two-point experiment in the remaining regimes. The product-Poisson experiment is only an auxiliary lower experiment: under \(\mathbb P_{\mathbf z}^{\mathrm{sp}}\) its total count has mean \(BnS(\mathbf z)\), and conditional on that total its labels are independent with law \(\mathbb P_{\mathbf z}^{\mathrm{sp}}\). Project any fixed-sample estimator to \([0,1]\), which cannot increase squared loss, and apply it to the first \(n\) labels whenever the total is at least \(n\). Since \(S(\mathbf z)\ge1/2\) and \(B>2\), the uniform shortage probability is at most \(\exp\{-n(B-2)^2/(4B)\}\). Thus an auxiliary Poisson lower bound transfers to the exactly \(n\)-observation risk after this explicit bounded-loss correction; the two experiments are not identified.

items.label: Theorem T-4
items.nl: there are universal constants \(0<c_\star\le C_\star<\infty\) such that, for every \(n\ge1\), \(d\ge2\), and \(0<\epsilon\le1/2\), \[c_\star\min\left\{1,\frac{d}{n\epsilon L_d}\right\}\le\mathfrak R_{n,d,\epsilon}\le\sup_{\mathbb P\in\mathcal D_{d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{obs}}}E_{\mathbb P}[(\widehat V_{n,d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{AF}}-\Psi(\mathbb P))^2]\le C_\star\min\left\{1,\frac{d}{n\epsilon L_d}\right\}.\] Through Proposition 1, the same frontier holds for \(V^\star(P)\) over causal completions. This strictly extends the archived fixed-overlap theorem by making the comparison constants universal over shrinking \(\epsilon\).

items.label: Theorem T-5
items.nl: along every triangular sequence \(n\to\infty\), \(d=d_n\ge2\), and \(0<\epsilon=\epsilon_n\le1/2\), uniform consistency for \(\Psi(\mathbb P)\) over \(\mathcal D_{d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{obs}}\) is possible if and only if \[\frac{d}{n\epsilon\log(ed)}\longrightarrow0.\] For each fixed \(d\), the risk reduces to order \(\min\{1,(n\epsilon)^{-1}\}\), and for each fixed positive \(\epsilon\) the result reduces to the archived \(\min\{1,d/[n\log(ed)]\}\) frontier.

items.label: Theorem T-6
items.nl:
There are universal constants \(0<c<C<\infty\) such that, for every \(K\geq2\), \(2\leq M\leq K^2\), and \(0\leq\epsilon\leq1/2\),
\[
 c\frac{\sqrt M}{K}
 \leq \mathcal E_{K,M,\epsilon}^{w}
 \leq \Delta_{K,M,\epsilon}
 \leq 4\mathcal E_{K,M,\epsilon}^{w}
 \leq C\frac{\sqrt M}{K}.
\]
The lower inequality is attained, up to the universal constant, by the explicit Jackson-packet pair of probability measures constructed in the proof; that pair is supported on \([0,M]\), has common first moment exactly one, and matches every moment through degree \(K\).  Thus there is no \(\epsilon\)-elbow on \([0,1/2]\) and no additional \(M\)-elbow on \([2,K^2]\): fixed \(M\) gives order \(K^{-1}\), \(M=o(K^2)\) gives the interpolating order \(\sqrt M/K=o(1)\), and \(M\asymp K^2\), including \((\epsilon,M)=(0,K^2)\), gives order one.

Consequently, there are universal constants \(0<c_\star\leq C_\star<\infty\) such that, for every \(n\geq1\), \(d\geq2\), and \(0<\epsilon\leq1/2\),
\[
 c_\star\min\left\{1,\frac{d}{n\epsilon\log(ed)}\right\}
 \leq \mathfrak R_{n,d,\epsilon}
 \leq
 \sup_{\mathbb P\in\mathcal D_{d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{obs}}}
 E_{\mathbb P}\!\left[
 \{\widehat V_{n,d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{AF}}-\Psi(\mathbb P)\}^2
 \right]
 \leq C_\star\min\left\{1,\frac{d}{n\epsilon\log(ed)}\right\}.
\]
Through the stated identification result, the same frontier holds for the causal value \(V^\star(P)\).  Along a triangular sequence, uniform consistency is possible if and only if
\[
 \frac{d}{n\epsilon\log(ed)}\longrightarrow0.
\]
